summary: Pair 03 (Lesson 3 + Worksheet 3) passes round 2 at the high bar. ALIGNMENT: A6.12 is the keystone primary; A6.10 and A6.11 are explicitly threaded through stories and the keyword chart; curriculum_expectations text is byte-identical to input_row.json; the lesson bridges back to Lesson 2's number bonds (recycled partners-of-5 for emerging) and forward to Lesson 5's Snack Shop. PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH: the trap (right answer, wrong operation) is anchored in Carpenter & Moser CGI (1983) Join/Separate Result-Unknown taxonomy, Riley & Greeno (1988) schema-recognition vs direct-modelling, and Fuson (1992) word-problem strategy progression; recovery_moves are 3-way diagnostic-branched (DIAGNOSTIC A wrong-sign-but-right-answer keyword-from-chart-before-sign; B mis-models-START physically build start with cubes; C can't-identify-keyword two-corner body-trace ADD/TAKE-AWAY corners). INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE: every required material is everyday (snap-cubes, ten-frames, picture cards, anchor chart, pennies); puppets explicitly OPTIONAL with substitution path (stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures); 8/22/10 timing equals 40 minutes — within the K 30-40 cap; differentiation.for_movement_learners offers a NO-PAPER, NO-CUBE PATH using two-corner acted-out story corners and bodies. CLARITY_VOICE: Penny refrain 'STORY first — SIGN next — COUNT last! That's how Penny shops!' chanted 3x with claps in BOTH minds_on (after the cube demo) and consolidation/exit_routine — the distinctive memorable chant the children carry between lessons; all success_criteria start with 'I can'; vocabulary defined child-friendly. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY: conceptual progression is explicit (story to schema to operation to model to equation); strategy-compare moment in action.steps[4] (two pairs share same story solved at cube vs ten-frame stations; class debates which felt fastest while affirming the OPERATION is the same regardless of tool); misconceptions named in CGI / Riley & Greeno / Fuson research-grounded terms. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY: every worksheet part maps to a named success criterion (Part 1 -> decide if I add or take away; Part 2 -> show the start of the story with cubes via START/CHANGE/END boxes; Part 3 -> write the answer as a number sentence by reverse-generating a story); Part 3 deliberately VARIES the practice format (story-builder transfer task — child generates own story to match a given equation rather than rote repeat) and the variation is justified by the mid-unit formative purpose; image_assets reference the lesson's manipulatives (snap-cubes, pennies, START/CHANGE/END boxes). All six categories cleared the Level 4 bar — round-2 lifts (Penny refrain in both bookends, Carpenter & Moser/Riley & Greeno/Fuson citations, 3-way diagnostic-branched recovery_moves, NO-PAPER NO-CUBE movement path, strategy-compare step) all landed.
